The height is given by

\[
y = 40t - 16t^2
\]

Velocity is the derivative of height with respect to time:

\[
v = \frac{dy}{dt} = 40 - 32t
\]

Substitute \(t = 2\):

\[
v = 40 - 32(2) = 40 - 64 = -24
\]

So the velocity is \(-24 \text{ ft/s}\).

The answer is (I)

\[
a_c=\frac{v^2}{r}
\]

\[
120\ \text{mi/hr} = 120 \times \frac{5280\ \text{ft}}{3600\ \text{s}} = 176\ \text{ft/s}
\]

Then:

\[

\]

The answer is (H)
